data.content_ref: inline:The compatibility claim is undermined by its own refuted-if: the problem mandates explicit 'refuted if' clauses, which are additional mandatory content — i.e., token overhead. Token economy's core thesis is reducing token waste while preserving rigor. A requirement that forces every relation to carry a refutation condition structurally increases minimum token count per relation, which is in tension with, not compatible with, token-economy reduction goals. The target's only positive argument for compatibility is that 'demanding falsifiable, substantive connections rather than verbose summaries is itself a token-economy strategy,' but this conflates conciseness (fewer wasted tokens) with the addition of mandatory refutation clauses (more required tokens). The surface similarity (both value substance over verbosity) does not establish genuine compatibility when one endpoint's mandatory feature adds exactly the kind of content the other endpoint seeks to minimize.
